observed: The page requests the admin-scoped TMDB token endpoint as soon as it mounts, even when the current browser session has no recent local-password proof.
The server correctly rejects that request with HTTP 403, but the page exposes the rejection as a generic error instead of an intentional reauthentication state.
Nested settings pages use the shared card and page-heading primitives but currently sit flush against the new white settings workspace, while the settings overview supplies its own inset spacing.
target: Do not request the protected token endpoint until the frontend session state shows the assurance required by the server.
Present a clear password-confirmation state with a real route to the existing account reauthentication form, while keeping the actual token load and save flows intact after confirmation.
Give non-overview settings pages consistent workspace insets through the settings layout without changing individual forms or controls.
boundaries: Frontend only; no authentication, API, database, dependency, or server changes.
Do not read, log, capture, or expose the token or error response content.
Keep permission filtering, part filtering, keyboard navigation, mobile section picker, and every existing settings page available.
